comment: Great guy who's been at UR forever. Just an overall decent man too- kind, straightforward and class is pretty easy if you attend and do problem sets. Definitely take Hoke!

I am not very good in math and didnt take calc in HS, but I thought this class was fine. Dr. Hoke lets you retake quizzes you didnt do well on, and is generally good with being available to help you out. Not a huge fan of the WebAssign HW, but he does give you lots of review/practice resources that are very helpful on the tests.

Harry Hoke is a great guy. He helped me whenever I needed it, but those who took Calc in HS will be better prepared. He is a fair and respected professor, who has been at UR forever and whose wife is in charge of the Math Dept. If you are prepared for class, attend all lectures and study for the tests, you should be able to get an A.

Homework easy and not too much, tests 75% easy and not too long. All he does is teaching, in monotone. No chitchat, no jokes. Can be mesmerizing from time to time, but he is never confusing and is always passionate about math. Recommend to people interested in math/science rather than fulfilling gen ed requirements.
Dr. Hoke is very nice and accomodating during the COVID-19 crisis. Tests are very fair and based on homework.
He is a caring guy and really nice, one of the better math professors at UR, but very average

Hoke is a good teacher. Calc is pretty straight forward and he teaches it that way. He explains things pretty clearly and will help you if you go to his office. he will let you take the skill quizzes as many times as you want until you get the grade that you want, which is great. Tests are mostly pretty good as long as you do the work and practice

Hoke is a good teacher. Calc is pretty straight forward and he teaches it that way. He explains things pretty clearly and will help you if you go to his office. he will let you take the skill quizzes as many times as you want until you get the grade that you want, which is great. Tests are mostly pretty good as long as you do the work and practice.

No pop quizzes. Lectures will be nothing like HW, but TESTS/QUIZZES WILL LOOK LIKE HW. Don't even bother buying the textbook, it's not useful. He's a really nice guy but and will try to help you out of class (but often to no avail). He IS fair, but be ready to learn LOTS OF NEW AND APPLICATIONS even if you took calc in high school and did well.

I missed like ten classes and nothing happened to me. If you're taking calc, take Hoke. He's super easy. Quizzes can be retaken for full credit. I have not done the HW in two months and still have a reasonable shot at an A. Super nice dude too. Warning not to take his 8am. You won't show up.

Dr. Hoke is the perfect professor for Calc 1 (if you took it in high school). He tends to lecture about the concept without giving many examples, and the homework often includes difficult variations on the concept. He's really helpful in office hours though and also a super nice person.

Being honest, Hoke isn't the greatest calc teacher. I took calc 1 in high school, and I pretty much use all of my past knowledge to do the work in this class. That being said, he's a super nice guy. You can retake quizzes as many times as you want until you're satisfied with the grade and the tests are not bad at all.

Hoke is a nice professor and doesn't assign mandatory homework. The tests were fair because they covered class material so if you show up and listen you should get an A. There is a quiz every Friday which makes people actually show up for class but they are so easy and a grade boost.
He explains the material well and makes the information make sense. There are weekly quizzes, so make sure you are on top of the material. Gives lots of opportunities for practice of the materials.

Harry (or Chip) Hoke is a really nice teacher. If you meet with him outside of class he is very helpful. I had taken calc in high school, but did not do very well in his class because there are only 3 tests and the final which comprise your entire grade (there are 2 quizzes and homework but they barely count). Not a good test taker?-- beware

Professor Hoke is a great guy and he will help you if you go to his office hours. But get ready to do a lot of learning by yourself because you barely learn anything from his lectures. Without introducing a subject and providing any notes or definitions, he will just go straight into examples when starting a new chapter. Frustrating class.

Harry (or Chip, that's the name he goes by) is a great professor, and will do everything in his power to help you pass the class. He is always available to meet with outside of class and is very flexible. He can get a bit confusing, and his explanations almost always leave me more puzzled than before I asked him, but overall he's a great prof.
Dr. Hoke is eager to help for students who ask. Just be sure to ace the tests because they are your only hope for an A; he hardly gives any credit to the homework.

I liked Dr. Hoke. Sure, the class wasn't interesting, but he's the guy to get Calc out of the way. Fairly clear, has office hours if you need. Posts old tests which are similar to the ones he gives. I didn't take calc and I found his class easy. Final replaces lowest grade, which is nice. Good grading system. He's a bit dull so take his class later
He is a good guy but is not very good at explaining concepts to students. I have heard that he is helpful outside of class, but I never went to him for extra help.

He's a nice guy, but he requires students to be really independent and teaches the class as if everyone had already taken it in high school. Everyone who already took Calculus in high school is doing significantly better than those of us who did not. The tests are also significantly harder than the homework and there is a lot of nightly work.

You get what you put in in this class. His tests are easier than the homework but the homework is a lot! Not that hard of an A if you have taken the class before. I would definitely recommend him, if you have.

He is very nice and is always smiling, however, I did not like the way he taught the class. Many times he depends on the students to work on their own and get it right, but that is very hard in Calc I. He is helpful if you ask, but his tests were hard. There is a lot of homework but there is not enough time in class to go over it. Tough teacher!
always wear a smile on his face. half-hour homework each time. easy class for Chinese.
He is a great guy. However, I am not sure if he is the professor to go for Calc 1. He is reasonable in terms of grades but I would only recommend him if you have taken Calc 1 in high school

Does a great job explaining stuff in class, homework is a lot, at least an hour and a half, but it is usually straight forward stuff , you have to go to class, because each hw is graded and if you miss on class, you cant hand in hw and that can ruin your grade, tests are challenging but not impossible

Easygoing teacher, very good refresher class for anyone who's taken Calculus in high school. If not, he's very helpful outside of class and answers any questions during class, even the stupid ones. Test aren't too bad, he drops the bottom five or so homework grades, and his grading scale is a bit easier than most.

He is extremely good at what he does and explains the material really well.  Calculus was my weakness, but after taking his class, it has become my strength.  He is very systematic, coherent and helpful.  Take him if you've had little or no prior experience and want to develop a strong basic pool of calculus concepts.

Hoke can get off track sometimes and go quick through the material, but he is helpful in his office hours in explaining homework.  He is also very straightforward in his tests also and are easier than the homeworks.  Overall, a fair grader and helpful outside of class.
Prof Hoke is helpful outside of class, but in class, I felt he went very quickly through the material. Tests were much harder than the weekly quizzes. Overall, not bad for fulfilling the FSSR gened.

Hoke is one of the worst professors i have ever had. If you have not taken calc before- DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. He does not explain anything well. It only makes sense to people who I have prior background in clac. Those people end up getting 100s on almost everything. The rest of the class is stuck wondering whats going on.
good teacher. very easy.

This class requires a lot of independent student. His homework assignments take a very long time and are worth a significant portion of your final grade. He offers flexible office hours, but sometimes it's not very helpful. You have to do a lot of practice problems to do well.

So helpful! Goes out of his way to explain the material and does it in a way that is clear and relatable. I am not a math person and was worried about taking a math course but he has made this course so enjoyable.

Such a wonderful teacher! He is beyond helpful and teaches with enthusiasm. So kind and always does everything he can to help his students. If you go to his class, and pay attention, you are sure to do well. He gives a quiz every Fri which may seem like a bad thing but they are only worth 10 points and by the time the tests comes you are prepared!
dr. hoke is the best teacher ever! I never understood calculus in high school, but he makes it all so clear! LOVE this class!

Dr. Hoke is awesome!he can explain the things very well. and it is easy to catch up with his class. always willing to help us!and his tests are not that hard if you pay attention to his homework and pastpapers

Hoke was a great teacher. He was always so helpful, and if he wasnt clear, he always made sure you understood it during office hours. His tests are fair and you could really tell that he cared. I'd recommend him.
My favorite teacher of the semester!  Definitely take Dr. Hoke, he is a quality teacher.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU HAVE NEVER HAD CALCULUS BEFORE!!! I saw way too many people failing because they had never taken calc. For those of you who have taken calc, Hoke is an easy professor and teaches his calc class for students who have had experience in the subject. He as three tests, Friday quizzes, and a final.

He is a great guy.  If you study and work at it, you can do well.  However, if you have zero experience in the class beforehand, I understand how this may be a hard class for you.  The class is kind of taught for kids who have already taken it which is why I found it easy and enjoyed him as a teacher.
Worst professor I've had. He rushes through his lectures and only half teaches. When you ask questions sometimes he doesn't completely answer them. Please do yourself a favor and don't take him.

This teacher makes your core experience horrible! If you have the choice choose someone else to be your core teacher. He approaches literature from a mathematical perspective, which means he has no idea how to interpret the books.
A nice guy, but if you haven't taken Calc before you seriously cannot get a good grade in this class. Do NOT take him if you haven't taken Calculus previously.
Nice guy, but if you haven't taken Calc before do not take his class
His poor future core students. He grades papers like a math teacher. Actually, approaches everything like a math teacher (sometimes useful, usually not). Also makes students do daily reading logs.

Take this class if you took calc in high school. He is good at reinforcing things already learned, but not necessarily at new topics. Homework is not graded, unlike in other calc classes, but it helps if you do it. a very nice guy.

Dr. Hoke is a great teacher.  If you read the book and ask questions is class, you'll do fine.  DO THE HOMEWORK....he frequently takes questions just like the homework for tests.  If you can do the homework, an A on any 4 of his tests are easily attainable.  Also, do the practice tests and all other sheets...they help alot...really a great guy, too
He is really easy if you actually bother doing homework. Most people dont, and get C's. You can get an easy A by reading.

He's a relatively easy A if you took some Calculus in high school. However, you may struggle if you've had little exposure to Calculus. He doesn't give too much homework.There are 3 tests, a final exam, and a few small quizzes.

Dr. Hoke is a great teacher who has a passion for teaching and for mathematics. He has a very sophisticated sense of humor...I find all of his jokes extremely funny. I have repeated many of them to my friends! (Who also enjoyed them)

Everybody above is bitter because they suck at math.  He's a great guy who enjoys his subject and is willing to give any amt. of time in order to make sure his students learn.  He is clear with what he does and does not deserve to be attacked like above.
I don' think he's that bad-you just have to learn to ask questions.  He doesn't have enough time to explain everything in class
He is not that bad. These other reviews are too harsh. Granted he is not "easy," but you have to be able to understand the concepts of calculus. If you do, you will do well in his class.

Worst teacher ever...I used to be good at math and now I feel like a retard because I cant understand anything he is trying to teach.  Its pointless to even go to class because you have to teach yourself everything and I thoroughly regret not saving my calc notes from highschool.

He's a horrible teacher, and his examples make no sense.  Everyone is confused by the end of class and he never explains how to do the homework problems he just goes through the numbers instead of the thought process.  He thinks he's hilarious, but no one else thinks so.

Horrible teacher.  Laughs at his own horrendous joke and really should just stop teaching.  He just can't teach and just confuses people.  I feel bad for those poor souls who have never taken calc before.  STAY AWAY
